headline: Entertainment venues where robots serve coffee and humanoids dance to K-pop are spreading across South Korea, Nikkei Asia reports.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a reputable outlet's trend report on robots reaching the public, but only the opening lines could be read.
importance_line: It shows South Korean robot startups trying to earn money from visitors rather than only from factories, as at Galaxy Robot Park in Seoul, which opened in August 2026, but it is not yet clear how many such venues exist or whether they turn a profit.
summary: Nikkei Asia reports that venues using robots driven by physical AI, meaning AI that controls machines acting in the real world, are spreading across South Korea, from robot baristas to humanoids dancing to K-pop alongside people, as startups look for income beyond manufacturing.
notes: Paywalled: only the sub-headline, photo caption and first paragraph were read. No other outlet carries this article. Galaxy Robot Park detail comes from the Nikkei photo caption.
